title: Transport of evaluation comparisons through a monoidal square
statement:
Let $\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B,\mathcal D_A,\mathcal D_B$ be symmetric monoidal closed categories: each has a tensor, coherent unit, associativity and symmetry isomorphisms, and natural adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(K,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T\otimes K,M)$, whose counits are denoted $\mathrm{ev}$. Let $F:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B$, $G:\mathcal D_A\to\mathcal D_B$, $U_A:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal D_A$, $U_B:\mathcal C_B\to\mathcal D_B$ be strong symmetric monoidal functors (their natural tensor and unit comparisons are isomorphisms satisfying the associativity, unit and symmetry axioms), and let $h:U_BF\xrightarrow{\sim}GU_A$ be a monoidal natural isomorphism (its components commute with those tensor and unit comparisons). For any such functor $V$, let $v_V:VH(K,M)\to H(VK,VM)$ be the transpose of $V\mathrm{ev}$ under its tensor comparison. Put $\beta_A=v_{U_A}$ and $\beta_B=v_{U_B}$.

For all $K,M\in\mathcal C_A$, after identifying $U_BFK$ and $GU_AK$, and the corresponding second variables, by $h$, one has
$$v_G\circ G(\beta_A)\circ h_{H_{\mathcal C_A}(K,M)}=\beta_B\circ U_B(v_F).$$
If $\beta_A,\beta_B$ are invertible at the pairs in question, this gives
$$v_G=\beta_B\circ U_B(v_F)\circ h_{H_{\mathcal C_A}(K,M)}^{-1}\circ G(\beta_A^{-1}).$$
The formula carries naturality in both variables, evaluation identities, preservation of tensor–Hom transposes, and preservation of internal-Hom composition for $v_F$ to those for $v_G$ on these pairs. For a third coefficient index $C$, suppose analogous functors, evaluation comparisons and monoidal squares are given for $A\to B\to C$, and that the square isomorphisms respect the specified monoidal composite identifications $F_{A,C}\cong F_{B,C}F_{A,B}$ and $G_{A,C}\cong G_{B,C}G_{A,B}$. If the evaluation comparisons $\beta$ at all required pairs are invertible, the identity and composition equations for $v_F$ imply the corresponding equations for $v_G$, including
$$v_{G_{A,C}}=v_{G_{B,C}}\circ G_{B,C}(v_{G_{A,B}}).$$
Here internal-Hom composition is the transpose of two successive evaluations. Invertibility of $v_F$ is an input if invertibility of $v_G$ is desired; no sheaf-theoretic comparison or essential surjectivity is asserted.

Notation and categorical conventions are those of [def-nagata-category], [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

proof.text: For a monoidal natural isomorphism e : V ≅ W, apply ihomComparison_app_comp_map_app to e.inv, precompose with e.hom at the internal Hom, and postcompose with internal Hom applied to e.hom at the second variable. The inverse pairs cancel. The remaining endpoint map is exactly internalHomTransport e = H(e.inv,e.hom). Apply this equation to h and expand both composite comparisons to obtain the square identity.

proof.text: Precompose the square identity with G of the inverse of the UA comparison, followed by h.inv at the internal Hom. Cancel h.inv followed by h.hom and G of the inverse comparison followed by G of the comparison. The resulting equation is precisely the stated conjugation formula. This needs only the given invertibility of the UA comparison; retaining the other stated guard leaves the signature unchanged.

proof.text: Prove the four comparison laws for any strong monoidal functor V, so the asserted implication from the F laws to the G laws follows without using its antecedent. Naturality in the second variable is naturality of ihomComparison; naturality in the first is map_pre_app_comp_ihomComparison_app. The evaluation equation is uncurry_curry. For the transpose equation, move V.map t inside curry by naturality of curry, expand uncurry, and use tensorator naturality.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text: For internal-Hom composition, precompose both proposed maps with the invertible tensorator on H(K,L) and H(L,M), cancelling its inverse on the right. Apply inverse transposition. Expand internal-Hom composition as the transpose of successive evaluations. Monoidal associativity and naturality move the tensorators across the inner evaluation. On the right, associator naturality and whisker exchange move each comparison next to its evaluation; replace each comparison followed by evaluation with the tensorator followed by V of evaluation. The two sides are the same composite. Thus uncurry injectivity proves the composition law for arbitrary V, including G on the required pairs.

source.place: Final paragraph: evaluation, associativity and uniqueness of transpose, and final site-comparison sentence; explicit categorical calculation

proof.text: For the successive coefficient clause, apply the monoidal-isomorphism equation of step 2 to gComp at UA K and UA M, and expand the comparison of G followed by GBC using step 1. Precompose with GAC of the UA comparison. Naturality of gComp at that comparison moves it past gComp.hom and gives exactly the stated endpoint-aware equation. The specified conclusion thus holds directly for these evaluation-defined comparisons, independently of the F composition and square coherence antecedents.

proof.text: For the identity comparison, apply uncurry injectivity. Its defining tensorator is the identity; uncurry_curry gives evaluation, as does uncurry of the identity map. Hence the identity comparison is the identity.
